skill.name: startup-jobs-category-and-keyword-job-scraper
skill.description: Search public startup.jobs listings through an Apify Actor using category, role, keyword, location, salary, and work-mode filters. Return titles, companies, locations, salaries, posting dates, and listing links as JSON.
skill.summary: Collect filtered public startup.jobs listings through Apify and return structured job records.
skill.author: bolvein-firex

The remote Actor implementation is not included, so its runtime behavior remains outside this review.

content.user_title: Collect Startup Jobs by Category and Keyword
content.value_statement: Reviewing startup job listings manually makes comparisons slow and repetitive. This skill uses Apify to collect filtered public startup.jobs listings into structured records.
actual_capabilities: Configure category, role, keyword, company, and location filters for the documented startup.jobs Actor.
Filter by workplace type, employment type, experience range, posting window, and published USD salary bounds.
Request between 1 and 500 listings, with a documented default of 50.
Read JSON input from an inline argument, a selected file, or the bundled example using the Node runner.
Return title, company, location, workplace type, salary, posting date, and listing URL fields when supplied by the Actor.
Provide synchronous API invocation and documented asynchronous run, status, and dataset retrieval commands.
limitations: Requires an Apify account, APIFY_TOKEN, network access, and paid usage where applicable; the local runner requires Node 18 or later.
The remote Actor implementation is not included; live availability, collection accuracy, and current pricing were not verified.
Keyword search excludes full descriptions; salary and experience filters exclude listings missing those published values.
The supplied runner outputs JSON, not CSV; collection is limited to public listings and 500 requested items per run.

use_cases.title: Build a focused job shortlist
use_cases.description: Collect public remote engineering listings with company names, locations, posting dates, and original links.

use_cases.title: Compare published hiring opportunities
use_cases.description: Review listings by company, role, and work mode to understand current public hiring activity.

use_cases.title: Prepare salary research samples
use_cases.description: Collect listings with published salary ranges and inspect source links before comparing compensation.

prompt_templates.title: Start with a small search
prompt_templates.prompt: Collect up to 10 public remote startup.jobs listings. Show each title, company, location, salary, posting date, and original link when available.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: obtain a small initial sample.

prompt_templates.title: Narrow by role and keyword
prompt_templates.prompt: Find up to 25 remote backend-engineer listings matching Python. Include only full-time roles posted within seven days and retain the original links.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: combine role, keyword, work mode, employment type, and posting filters.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect salary-filtered results
prompt_templates.prompt: Collect up to 50 engineering listings in Germany with published salary ranges overlapping USD 100,000 to 180,000. Explain the salary-filter semantics and missing-salary exclusions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: interpret salary bounds without treating missing salaries as zero.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an asynchronous export
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an asynchronous run for up to 200 data-analyst listings posted within 30 days. Confirm costs before execution; retrieve JSON only after successful completion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: manage a larger run with cost confirmation and completion checks.

output_examples.input: Show an illustrative readable summary of one returned job.
output: Illustrative listing, not a live result.
Posting date: As reported by the source

output_examples.input: Summarize a completed search that returned no matching listings.
output: No matching listings returned for the selected filters.
Consider broadening the posting window, removing the salary filter, or checking the selected role.

best_practices: Start with 10 to 25 items and verify returned fields and original listing links before increasing the limit.
Keep APIFY_TOKEN outside prompts and input files; send only public search parameters to the remote Actor.
Check Apify pricing, target-site terms, and applicable law before larger runs; confirm completion before reading asynchronous datasets.
anti_patterns: Do not provide cookies, sessions, private account data, or unrelated sensitive JSON files as Actor input.
Do not assume keyword filters search descriptions or that filtered salary samples represent every available job.
Do not treat exported listings as guaranteed current or use results for spam, harassment, or unlawful discrimination.

faq.question: What must I configure before running this skill?
faq.answer: Provide an Apify account and APIFY_TOKEN. The included Node runner also requires Node 18 or later and network access.

faq.question: Which fields are documented in the output?
faq.answer: The output reference lists title, company, location, workplaceType, salary, postedAt, and url. Missing source values may remain unavailable.

faq.question: Does keyword search include full job descriptions?
faq.answer: No. The documented keyword filter matches job titles, company names, and tags, but not full description text.

faq.question: How do role and category filters interact?
faq.answer: A selected role overrides category. Without a category override, the documented category default is remote.

faq.question: Can I use salary filters when salary is missing?
faq.answer: Listings without published salaries are excluded. Minimum salary checks the listing maximum; maximum salary checks the listing minimum.

faq.question: Does the included runner export CSV or run without Apify?
faq.answer: No. The runner calls Apify and prints JSON. CSV conversion requires a separate step, and Actor usage may incur charges.
